# Studio tools

The multi-agent studio: roster, board, feedback, decisions, loops, messages and playtests.

25 tools in the `studio` category. Badges: **read-only** tools never change the project; **mutating** tools are undoable and attributed; **open-world** tools reach outside the engine and MCP clients ask before running them.

| Tool | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`studio_overview`](#studio_overview) | Start here when working with the studio (a team of AI agents making this game). |
| [`studio_agent_define`](#studio_agent_define) | Create a studio agent or update one (by id or name; only the fields you pass change). |
| [`studio_agent_list`](#studio_agent_list) | The studio roster: each agent's id (use it for assignees and @mentions), name, role, discipline, focus, live status, open tasks and usage. |
| [`studio_agent_brief`](#studio_agent_brief) | Everything needed to *be* a roster member: its system prompt (role mission, focus, persona, standing instructions, memory, the team, studio etiquette) and the engine tools it may use with their access (allow \| ask). |
| [`studio_agent_remove`](#studio_agent_remove) | Remove an agent from the studio (deletes agents/&lt;id&gt;.agent.json; its open tasks become unassigned). |
| [`studio_team_template`](#studio_team_template) | Spawn a whole team of specialists from a template (agents that already exist by id are updated): starter_crew (5 generalists), indie_trio (3), aaa_strike_team (22: director, producer, five designers, four programmers, five artists, audio, writing, QA, two playtester personas, critic), narrative_team, qa_squad (QA lead, three playtester personas, critic, fixer), art_team, audio_team. |
| [`studio_memory`](#studio_memory) | Your long-term memory as a studio agent (kept in your profile and shown at the start of every task): note a fact worth remembering (conventions, decisions, the human's preferences, unfinished work), forget an outdated note by number, or list notes. |
| [`studio_usage_report`](#studio_usage_report) | Record tokens an agent spent with its own model, for studio budgets and cost tracking (runners that call models outside the engine — the editor crew, custom scripts — report each request here). |
| [`studio_task_create`](#studio_task_create) | Put a task on the studio board. |
| [`studio_task_update`](#studio_task_update) | Move a task across the board (backlog → todo → doing → review → done, or dropped), reassign it, edit it, or add a comment. |
| [`studio_task_list`](#studio_task_list) | The studio board. |
| [`studio_task_claim`](#studio_task_claim) | Claim a task and start it (assignee = you, status = doing). |
| [`studio_feedback_submit`](#studio_feedback_submit) | File feedback about the game as a playtester, critic, agent or human: category (fun, difficulty, clarity, visuals, audio, performance, bug, narrative, accessibility), severity, a one-line summary, details, what it's about (target), and evidence {playtest: "P-3", captures: [...], metrics: {...}, positions: [[x,y,z]], repro: [steps]}. |
| [`studio_feedback_list`](#studio_feedback_list) | Feedback with each item's director verdict (act / drop / defer / merge_into), rationale and measured effect (metrics before/after). |
| [`studio_feedback_update`](#studio_feedback_update) | Change a feedback item: status (e.g. |
| [`studio_decide`](#studio_decide) | The director's (or producer's) verdict on a feedback item, visible to everyone with its rationale: act (creates tasks — give each a title, acceptance criteria and an assignee — or links existing task_ids), drop (won't do, say why), defer (later), or merge_into a duplicate. |
| [`studio_loop_define`](#studio_loop_define) | Define a studio loop: a repeatable cycle of stages with stop conditions, stored in studio/loops/&lt;name&gt;.loop.json. |
| [`studio_loop_start`](#studio_loop_start) | Start a run of a loop. |
| [`studio_loop_advance`](#studio_loop_advance) | Report the results of a loop stage's assignments and move the loop on: reports [{agent, report, signoff?, usage?}]. |
| [`studio_loop_status`](#studio_loop_status) | A loop's state: status, iteration, current stage, pending assignments (with prompts), per-iteration history (stage reports, playtests, filed feedback, verified effects) and metric trends. |
| [`studio_loop_stop`](#studio_loop_stop) | Stop a running loop (pending assignments are dropped). |
| [`studio_message_send`](#studio_message_send) | Talk to the team so the back-and-forth is visible: post in a channel (#general by default; any name creates a channel), address agents with `to` or @mentions in the text (@id, @role, @discipline, @all), reply in a thread with reply_to, and reference a task/feedback. |
| [`studio_inbox`](#studio_inbox) | Messages for you (addressed to you, mentioning you, or broadcast in #general), oldest first; unread only by default, and reading marks them read. |
| [`playtest_run`](#playtest_run) | Play the game with a bot in a sandbox copy of the scene (the scene you edit is untouched) and get a report: completion rate, time-to-goal, deaths and their causes, fails, damage, stuck periods, objectives, coverage, frame cost, screenshots at notable moments and a top-down heatmap (returned as an image). |
| [`playtest_compare`](#playtest_compare) | Before/after comparison of two playtests (ids like P-3): every metric with its delta and whether it got better or worse (direction-aware: fewer deaths is better, higher completion is better). |

### `studio_overview` { #studio_overview }

**Studio overview** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Start here when working with the studio (a team of AI agents making this game). Returns the roster with live status, the task board counts, feedback waiting for a decision, recent director decisions with measured effects, loops and their state, the latest playtest metrics, and token/cost usage. include_catalog=true also lists roles, disciplines, team templates and loop templates.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `include_catalog` | boolean |  | Also return roles, team templates and loop templates |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    studio_overview {"include_catalog": true}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call studio_overview '{"include_catalog": true}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "studio_overview",
        "arguments": {
          "include_catalog": true
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `studio_agent_define` { #studio_agent_define }

**Define agent** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Create a studio agent or update one (by id or name; only the fields you pass change). An agent is a specialist: a role (e.g. level_designer, gameplay_programmer, lighting_artist, playtester, critic — see studio_overview include_catalog), a focus (what exactly it owns: "enemy AI", "onboarding"), a persona, standing instructions, a model, an autonomy level (observe = read-only, ask = changes need human approval, autonomous), per-tool-category permissions (allow|ask|off), and who it reports to. Saved as agents/<id>.agent.json (shareable, git-friendly). Playtesters take persona knobs in playtest {policy, reaction_time, skill, curiosity, patience}. Example: {name:"Mira", role:"level_designer", focus:"secret areas", focus_tags:["secrets"], reports_to:"nimbus"}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  | Agent id to update (default: derived from name) |  |
| `name` | string |  | Display name |  |
| `role` | string |  | Role | `creative_director` `art_director` `producer` `systems_designer` `level_designer` `narrative_designer` `economy_designer` `ux_designer` `gameplay_programmer` `ai_programmer` `graphics_programmer` `tools_programmer` `environment_artist` `lighting_artist` `character_artist` `vfx_artist` `technical_artist` `ui_artist` `sound_designer` `composer` `writer` `qa_lead` `playtester` `critic` |
| `discipline` | string |  | Discipline (default: from the role) | `direction` `production` `design` `engineering` `art` `audio` `writing` `qa` |
| `focus` | string |  | What this agent specializes in |  |
| `focus_tags` | string[] |  | Short focus tags |  |
| `persona` | string |  | Personality / voice |  |
| `mission` | string |  | Replaces the role's built-in mission |  |
| `instructions` | string |  | Standing instructions: style guides, constraints, conventions |  |
| `provider` | string |  | anthropic \| openai \| mock \| an editor provider name |  |
| `model` | string |  | Model id (empty = provider default, e.g. claude-opus-5-5) |  |
| `autonomy` | string |  | How freely it may change the game | `observe` `ask` `autonomous` |
| `permissions` | object |  | Per tool category: {"network":"off","render":"ask"} |  |
| `reports_to` | string |  | Agent id of its lead |  |
| `color` | string |  | Avatar color #rrggbb |  |
| `face` | string |  | Avatar face | `happy` `focused` `dreamy` `wink` `determined` `curious` |
| `max_rounds` | integer |  | Max tool rounds per task (default 40) |  |
| `memory` | string[] |  | Replace its long-term memory notes |  |
| `playtest` | object |  | Playtester persona: {policy, reaction_time, skill, curiosity, patience} |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    studio_agent_define {"id": "level_designer", "name": "Mira", "role": "level_designer", "focus": "layout and pacing", "reports_to": "creative_director"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call studio_agent_define '{"id": "level_designer", "name": "Mira", "role": "level_designer", "focus": "layout and pacing", "reports_to": "creative_director"}' --project my_game
    ```

### `studio_agent_brief` { #studio_agent_brief }

**Agent brief** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Everything needed to *be* a roster member: its system prompt (role mission, focus, persona, standing instructions, memory, the team, studio etiquette) and the engine tools it may use with their access (allow | ask). Use it to run a studio agent in any harness: e.g. give a Claude Code / Codex subagent this system prompt, let it call only the listed tools, and connect it as "<client>/<agent id>" (or pass as: "<agent id>") so its work is attributed. loop_member=true withholds loop and roster control tools.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent` | string | yes | Agent id or name |  |
| `loop_member` | boolean |  | Running inside a loop stage |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    studio_agent_brief {"agent": "{{STUDIO_ID}}", "loop_member": true}
    ```

=== "CLI"


    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "studio_agent_brief",
        "arguments": {
          "agent": "{{STUDIO_ID}}",
    ```

### `studio_task_create` { #studio_task_create }

**Create task** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Put a task on the studio board. Good tasks are small and checkable: a clear title, acceptance criteria (how we know it's done), a discipline, and an assignee (agent id, or "@role" to pick the least busy agent with that role). Link the feedback it addresses so the effect can be measured. Example: {title:"Widen the lava bridge", acceptance:["bridge 3 m wide","deaths ≤ 1 per run"], assignee:"@level_designer", feedback:["F-2"]}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | yes | Short imperative title |  |
| `description` | string |  | Context and details |  |
| `acceptance` | string[] |  | Acceptance criteria, one per item |  |
| `discipline` | string |  | Discipline | `direction` `production` `design` `engineering` `art` `audio` `writing` `qa` |
| `assignee` | string |  | Agent id or @role |  |
| `priority` | string |  | Priority (default normal) | `low` `normal` `high` `critical` |
| `status` | string |  | Initial status (default todo) | `backlog` `todo` `doing` `review` `done` `dropped` |
| `depends_on` | string[] |  | Task ids that must be done first |  |
| `feedback` | string[] |  | Feedback ids this task addresses |  |
| `links` | object |  | Other links: {entities:["#12"], assets:[...], captures:[...]} |  |
| `as` | string |  | Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "&lt;client&gt;/&lt;agent id&gt;" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one. |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    studio_task_create {"title": "Widen the second canyon gap's landing", "discipline": "design", "priority": "high", "acceptance": ["Bots clear the gap in 3 of 3 runs"]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call studio_task_create '{"title": "Widen the second canyon gap'\''s landing", "discipline": "design", "priority": "high", "acceptance": ["Bots clear the gap in 3 of 3 runs"]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "studio_task_create",
        "arguments": {
          "title": "Widen the second canyon gap's landing",
          "discipline": "design",
          "priority": "high",
          "acceptance": [
            "Bots clear the gap in 3 of 3 runs"
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `studio_task_update` { #studio_task_update }

**Update task** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Move a task across the board (backlog → todo → doing → review → done, or dropped), reassign it, edit it, or add a comment. Marking the last task of a feedback item done moves that feedback to "fixed" (the next verification playtest then measures the effect). Moving to doing/done checks dependencies.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | string | yes | Task id, e.g. T-4 |  |
| `status` | string |  | New status | `backlog` `todo` `doing` `review` `done` `dropped` |
| `assignee` | string |  | Agent id (empty string unassigns) |  |
| `priority` | string |  | Priority | `low` `normal` `high` `critical` |
| `title` | string |  | Title |  |
| `description` | string |  | Description |  |
| `acceptance` | string[] |  | Acceptance criteria (replaces the list) |  |
| `discipline` | string |  | Discipline |  |
| `depends_on` | string[] |  | Replace dependencies |  |
| `links` | object |  | Links to add |  |
| `comment` | string |  | Comment for the thread (what changed, what's left) |  |
| `as` | string |  | Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "&lt;client&gt;/&lt;agent id&gt;" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one. |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    studio_task_update {"task": "T-12", "status": "review", "comment": "Landing widened by 1.5 m; playtest attached."}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call studio_task_update '{"task": "T-12", "status": "review", "comment": "Landing widened by 1.5 m; playtest attached."}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    ```

### `studio_task_claim` { #studio_task_claim }

**Claim task** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Claim a task and start it (assignee = you, status = doing). Without `task`, claims your highest-priority todo task, or else an unassigned todo task in your discipline. External agents identify with `as` or a client name ending in /<agent id>.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | string |  | Task id (default: pick the next one for you) |  |

### `studio_decide` { #studio_decide }

**Decide on feedback** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

The director's (or producer's) verdict on a feedback item, visible to everyone with its rationale: act (creates tasks — give each a title, acceptance criteria and an assignee — or links existing task_ids), drop (won't do, say why), defer (later), or merge_into a duplicate. The current playtest metrics are stored as the baseline, so the next verification playtest measures the effect (optionally against explicit targets like {"deaths":{"max":1}}); a regression reopens the tasks. Only direction/production agents (or humans) may decide. Example: {feedback:"F-2", verdict:"act", rationale:"Unfair spike", tasks:[{title:"Telegraph the lava", assignee:"@lighting_artist", acceptance:["glow visible from 10 m"]}]}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feedback` | string | yes | Feedback id |  |
| `verdict` | string | yes | Verdict | `act` `drop` `defer` `merge_into` |
| `rationale` | string | yes | Why — shown next to the feedback |  |
| `tasks` | object[] |  | Tasks to create (act) |  |
| `task_ids` | string[] |  | Existing tasks that address it (act) |  |
| `merge_into` | string |  | Feedback id it duplicates (merge_into) |  |
| `targets` | object |  | What success means: {metric: {min, max}} |  |
| `metrics_before` | object |  | Baseline metrics (default: latest playtest) |  |
| `redecide` | boolean |  | Override an earlier decision |  |
| `as` | string |  | Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "&lt;client&gt;/&lt;agent id&gt;" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one. |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    studio_decide {"feedback": "F-7", "verdict": "act", "rationale": "Unfair difficulty spike early in the level.", "targets": {"deaths": {"max": 1}}}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call studio_decide '{"feedback": "F-7", "verdict": "act", "rationale": "Unfair difficulty spike early in the level.", "targets": {"deaths": {"max": 1}}}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "studio_decide",
        "arguments": {
          "feedback": "F-7",
          "verdict": "act",
          "rationale": "Unfair difficulty spike early in the level.",
          "targets": {
            "deaths": {
              "max": 1
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `studio_loop_define` { #studio_loop_define }

**Define loop** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Define a studio loop: a repeatable cycle of stages with stop conditions, stored in studio/loops/<name>.loop.json. Start from a template (playtest_fix_verify, art_pass_with_critic, balance_tuning, vertical_slice_sprint, bug_bash) and override goal/stop, or write stages yourself. A stage is either kind "playtest" (the engine plays the game with bots: playtest {policy, runs, seconds}, file_feedback, verify_fixed) or kind "agents" (assignees: ["@role", "@discipline", "agent-id", "@a|@b" fallback], instruction template with {{goal}} {{inputs}} {{open_feedback}} {{my_tasks}} {{metrics}} {{roster}} {{iteration}}, parallel, only_with_tasks, gate {skip_if: no_open_feedback | no_todo_tasks | not_first_iteration | ..., approval: "human"}). stop: {max_iterations, metric_targets {completion_rate:{min:0.8}}, director_signoff, token_budget, time_budget_minutes}. delete=true removes it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | Loop name (default: the template's) |  |
| `template` | string |  | Start from this template | `playtest_fix_verify` `art_pass_with_critic` `balance_tuning` `vertical_slice_sprint` `bug_bash` |
| `goal` | string |  | What the loop is trying to achieve |  |
| `description` | string |  | Description |  |
| `stages` | object[] |  | Stages (replace the template's) |  |
| `stop` | object |  | Stop conditions (merged over the template's) |  |
| `delete` | boolean |  | Remove the loop |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    studio_loop_define {"template": "playtest_fix_verify", "goal": "Players finish the canyon run without unfair deaths"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call studio_loop_define '{"template": "playtest_fix_verify", "goal": "Players finish the canyon run without unfair deaths"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "studio_loop_define",
        "arguments": {
          "template": "playtest_fix_verify",
          "goal": "Players finish the canyon run without unfair deaths"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `studio_loop_advance` { #studio_loop_advance }

**Advance loop** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Report the results of a loop stage's assignments and move the loop on: reports [{agent, report, signoff?, usage?}]. When every pending assignment has reported (or complete_stage=true), the loop runs the following stages — playtests, verification, effect measurement — until it needs agents again, waits for approval, or ends on its stop conditions. Returns the new status with the next assignments. Directors sign off with signoff=true (or a report starting with SIGNOFF). approve=true/false answers a human approval gate.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `loop` | string | yes | Loop name |  |
| `reports` | object[] |  | Reports from the stage's agents |  |
| `approve` | boolean |  | Answer an approval gate |  |
| `signoff` | boolean |  | Director/producer sign-off for this iteration |  |
| `complete_stage` | boolean |  | Finish the stage even if some agents did not report |  |
| `as` | string |  | Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "&lt;client&gt;/&lt;agent id&gt;" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one. |  |

    ```json
            }
          ]
    ```

### `playtest_run` { #playtest_run }

**Playtest** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Play the game with a bot in a sandbox copy of the scene (the scene you edit is untouched) and get a report: completion rate, time-to-goal, deaths and their causes, fails, damage, stuck periods, objectives, coverage, frame cost, screenshots at notable moments and a top-down heatmap (returned as an image). Policies: goal_seeker (walks to entities tagged "goal"/"objective", avoids "hazard"/"enemy"), explorer (covers unexplored space), random, scripted (script: [{t: seconds, hold|release|press|click|event: ...}] — the same arguments as sim_input). persona {reaction_time, skill, curiosity, patience} shapes the bot; playtester agents use their own persona by default. runs>1 aggregates several seeds. Games should tag the player "player" and emit "death" / "fail" / "damage" / "objective" events. Saved under studio/playtests/<id>/; findings are returned for filing as feedback.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `policy` | string |  | Bot policy (default goal_seeker) | `goal_seeker` `explorer` `random` `scripted` |
| `seconds` | number |  | Simulated seconds per run (default 30, max 600) |  |
| `runs` | integer |  | Runs with consecutive seeds (default 1, max 20) |  |
| `seed` | integer |  | First seed (default 1) |  |
| `persona` | object |  | {reaction_time: s, skill: 0..1, curiosity: 0..1, patience: s} |  |
| `controls` | object |  | Key mapping {up, down, left, right, jump} (default w/s/a/d/space) |  |
| `script` | object[] |  | Input timeline (scripted policy) |  |
| `player` | integer \| string |  | Player entity (default: tagged "player") |  |
| `goal_radius` | number |  | Meters from a goal that count as reaching it (default 1) |  |
| `screenshots` | boolean |  | Capture screenshots (default true) |  |
| `screenshot_interval` | number |  | Also capture every N seconds |  |
| `max_screenshots` | integer |  | Screenshot cap (default 8) |  |
| `label` | string |  | Label for the report |  |
| `agent` | string |  | Use this playtester's persona |  |
| `include_heatmap` | boolean |  | Return the heatmap image (default true) |  |
| `as` | string |  | Act as this roster member (agent id). For external agents whose MCP client name isn't "&lt;client&gt;/&lt;agent id&gt;" (e.g. Claude Code subagents playing a role). Ignored when you already are one. |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    playtest_run {"policy": "goal_seeker", "runs": 3, "seconds": 45, "label": "before"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call playtest_run '{"policy": "goal_seeker", "runs": 3, "seconds": 45, "label": "before"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "playtest_run",
        "arguments": {
          "policy": "goal_seeker",
          "runs": 3,
          "seconds": 45,
          "label": "before"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    ```json
        }
      }
    }
    ```
